newsitem.title: CHINA: HK gold ends shade lower despite shortcovering.
newsitem.headline: HK gold ends shade lower despite shortcovering.

text.p: Hong Kong spot gold prices ended a shade lower on Monday from New York's previous close after shortcovering and European buying failed to erase earlier drops, dealers said.
Bullion ended at US$325.50/326.00 on Monday compared to New York's previous close at US$325.75/326.25 on Friday.
After opening weaker, some physical demand and shortcovering from Tokyo and Australia nudged gold prices up steadily in intraday trade to $325 per ounce, dealers said.
Early European buying interest in afternoon trade pushed gold up further from $325.00 per ounce to its closing price at $325.50/326.00 per ounce.
"It's been a pretty quite day with nothing special going on," said one source. Dealers saw gold testing slightly higher, but remaining range bound.
Hong Kong gold opened lower after Saturday's professional sales in the local market and selling from Japan, but recovered much of the losses in later activity, dealers said.
Local tael gold ended HK$7 up at HK$3,013.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society dropped to -5.50 from its previous fix at -5.00.
